paper.title: Lipschitz Bandits without the Lipschitz Constant

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic continuum-armed bandit on [0,1]^d with mean-payoff in F_{L,M} (Lipschitz, bounded Hessian)
unmapped: arm space is the hypercube [0,1]^d with Lipschitz continuity w.r.t. the l-infinity norm
f twice differentiable with |y^T H_f(x) y| <= M ||y||_inf^2 (Hessian bound M); L = max ||grad f||_1
learner knows neither L nor M
settings.definition_quote: We assume that $f$ is twice differentiable, with Hessians uniformly bounded by $M$ in the following sense: for all $\ux \in [0,1]^d$ and all $\uy \in [0,1]^d$, $| \uy^{T} H_f(\ux) \uy | \leq M \norm[\uy]_\infty^2$. ... In the sequel we denote by $\cF_{L,M}$ the set of environments whose mean-payoff functions satisfy the above assumption.

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic continuum-armed bandit on [0,1]^d with L-Lipschitz mean-payoff (F_L) (lower bound)
unmapped: arm space is the hypercube [0,1]^d with Lipschitz continuity w.r.t. the l-infinity norm
settings.definition_quote: We also denote by $\cF_{L}$ the larger set of environments whose mean-payoff functions $f$ is only constrained to be $L$--Lipschitz with respect to the $\ell^\infty$--norm.

algorithms.name: Two-phase strategy (uniform exploration to estimate L, then INF on adaptive discretization)

conditions: worst case over all L-Lipschitz (l-infinity) mean-payoff functions on [0,1]^d with rewards in [0,1]

source.label: th:LB
source.quote: For all strategies of the player and for all T \geq \max \{ L^d, ( \frac{0.15 L^{2/(d+2)}}{\max\{d,2\}} )^{d} \}, the worst-case regret over the set $\cF_{L}$ of all environments that are $L$--Lipschitz with respect to the $\ell^\infty$--norm is larger than \sup_{\cF_L} \oR_T \geq 0.15 \, L^{d/(d+2)}\,T^{(d+1)/(d+2)}.

results.notes: Adaptation of Bubeck et al. (X-armed bandits) Theorem 13; new as stated. Theorem number inferred as first theorem; no printed annotation. Regret defined via f(I_t), i.e. pseudo-regret.

symbols.m_bins: number of bins per direction in the pure exploration phase
symbols.E_explore: number of pulls per bin in the pure exploration phase

conditions: f in F_{L,M} (twice differentiable, Hessian bound M)
m >= 8*M_hess/L_lip (exploration grid fine enough relative to unknown M/L)
tuning: m (bins per direction) and E (pulls per bin) are free parameters

source.label: th:main
source.quote: When used with the multi-armed strategy INF, the strategy of Figure~\ref{fig:strat} ensures that \sup_{\cF_{L,M}} \oR_T \leq T^{(d+1)/(d+2)} ( 9 L^{d/(d+2)} + 5 ( 2 m\sqrt{\frac{2}{E} \ln ( 2 T^{d+1} )} )^{d/(d+2)} ) + E m^d + 2 \sqrt{2 T d^d} + 1 as soon as m \geq \frac{8 M}{L}.

results.notes: First part of the main theorem. Theorem number inferred. Algorithm uses T but not L or M.

bound.expression_latex: \max \{ ( \frac{8M}{L} + 1 )^{1/\alpha}, L^{d/(d+2)} T^{(d+1)/(d+2)} ( 9 + \varepsilon(T,d) ) \}, \ \varepsilon(T,d) = 5 T^{-\gamma} ( \ln ( 2T^d ) )^{d/(d+2)} + T^{-\gamma} + \frac{ 2\sqrt{2 d^d T} + 1}{T^{- (d+1)/(d+2)}}

conditions: f in F_{L,M} (twice differentiable, Hessian bound M)

source.label: th:main
source.quote: In particular, for 0 < \gamma < \frac{d(d+1)}{(3d+2)(d+2)} and \alpha = \frac{1}{d+2} ( \frac{d+1}{d+2} - \gamma \frac{3d+2}{d} ) > 0, the choices of m = \lfloor T^\alpha \rfloor and E = m^2 \lceil T^{2 \gamma (d+2)/d} \rceil yield the bound \sup_{\cF_{L,M}} \oR_T \leq \max \{ ( \frac{8M}{L} + 1 )^{1/\alpha}, L^{d/(d+2)} T^{(d+1)/(d+2)} ( 9 + \varepsilon(T,d) ) \}, where \varepsilon(T,d) = ... vanishes as T tends to infinity.

results.notes: The last term of epsilon(T,d) as printed divides by T^{-(d+1)/(d+2)}, which would not vanish; likely a typo for multiplication by T^{-(d+1)/(d+2)}. Recorded verbatim. Fully adaptive to L and M; needs T (doubling trick mentioned informally).
